title: ID0428824-DC/Si-D/CH[0bJm6K] - Volvo and MAN dont charge
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
MAN truck not charging properly and Volvo ERR67
Solution:
Update 26/Jun - RC swapped charger ID: 0bJm6K , with a warehouse charger ID: 3J90YB
For warranty purposes, we as TS, did not recommend such action. It was purely done by RC and not consulted with us before hand. We are not sure if this accounts as warranty anymore. Please do as you wish with this information.
Charger seems to have the same problem, so it's not fixed.
Update 2/Jul - Unfortunately we were not able to reproduce the error today. We will wait for feedback from the customer
Update 6/Jul - No errors again
Update 19/Aug - The new EVCC is working without any error (
00.16.81.0e.fa.50
) and the rest still have the problem
Update 28/Aug - Call with EcoG - discussions ongoing about being able to develop the SECC to be more robust to CP state changes. If VOlvo has a solution, we should go for it.
Update 9/Sep - No issues again with the Volvo that had the replacement. Since the solution is clear,

Dear Naim,
Thank you for reaching
out
to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center - ERK
Main Asset
:
MP / S9 170004103
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
0bJm6K
Problem Description
: Volvo and MAN trucks having interruptions with ERR67. PilotState C to B during charging.
Troubleshooting
:
I've checked this charger for the past week and here are my findings for the MAN truck:
​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​During the 30th March we were able to charge 3 times, with 2 of them transfering ~7kWh.
​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​I would like to schedule with the customer to do stress testing - test a lot of charging sessions to find a common point.
​​​​​​​The only session I could recover the EcoG logs was from yesterday and it wasn't able to pass ParameterDiscovery
For the Volvo trucks, we are already waiting for the feedback from one the colleagues from Volvo. He is on vacation so we won't get a reply until earliest next week.
​​​​​​​If you want to test this scenario, we would require an osciloscope to measure the CP and PP signal to understand where the drop is coming from, if it's the charger or the EV.
​​​​​​​The message we got from Volvo is that they are seeing a emergency shutdown from the charger side and we are stopping because the EV changes the PilotState to B during C-state.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
Let me know when it's possible to arrange some tests.
For future reference, your case number is
0428824
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim

additional_info.subject: NOTE FROM TS before intervention
additional_info.body:
Note from TS:
Volvo trucks is a known issue, email trend sent. When Volvo HQ is back they will reply.
Confirm with Cata from VI.
MAN truck needs to be clarified. It seems there were some tests with Heliox chargers where they are indeed monitoring the PP signal whereas we don't. Can it be that the PP signal voltage dropped?
Table from MAN:
MAN truck charged 1 time successfully, logs in timeline and one time failed. All the other sessions we are not able to know the root cause since there is no EcoG logs.
The session that failed, we can see that there is no response from the EVCC. In the pcap we see no requests

additional_info.subject: NOTE FROM VI (intervention)
additional_info.body:
Tested with Volvo only - No MAN trucks available for test.
Results show that there is an interference in the ground during charging. This causes the CP state to drop - has a lot of peaks, which results in a failed session that mentions PilotState C dropped to B while charging - Err67.
We changed the TxStopPoint from EnergyTransfer to PowerPathClosed in order to mitigate the problem, as when the session fails, the Volvo will automatically attempt to restart the session and will charge again.
Alignment with Volvo needed for further analysis. Volvo colleague in Switzerland is able to go on-site since it's close to the office but not able today. He is to go and reproduce the issue and make the necessary measurements.
All files are shared in the ticket. Pico measurements, EcoG/State logs and SCB logs

additional_info.subject: 0428824 - ID0428824-DC/Si-D/CH[0bJm6K] - Volvo and MAN dont charge CRM:02867000001
additional_info.body:
Hi Julian, good morning.
Since a few months (almost a year already), we have had the same issues that you are facing with Volvos, in several customers in Germany.
The problem with this error is that it's very sporadic and hard to reproduce, just like this week, we went on site and, unfortunately, didn't get any results from it.
From these same customers, we have this error since version v3.2.8, sometimes we have a full month of occurrences, and sometimes a full month without 1 single failed session.
From a discussion we had with a Volvo colleague from Germany (without any picoscope tests) is that the Volvo is requesting a stop due to a EVSE EmergencyShutdown, but the chargers clearly do not enter any emergency state.
That's why 2 weeks ago we planned to make measurements to bring to Volvo's attention and we got them, there is a noise on the signal which causes the CP line to drop and causes the session to stop.
Unfortunately, in that week when we got the error, there was no chance that the colleague from Volvo R&D to join us, so there was only a technician, which couldn't support us.
We already asked our R&D to give us any indications of measurements or ideas, to proceed with this topic.
Now, moving on to your message where the "original" charger still persists the error.
In this "
new
" charger there was already
12 occurrences
of the same error, that we saw in the "original" charger, which it has been monitored for the last 2 weeks:
As you can see, this problem is not solved with the new charger, it was just unfortunate that on the day of the tests, we were not able to reproduce it together with the support from Volvo R&D and the customer is not complaining, for now.
Since the "original" charger has been offline since it has been replaced we cannot say if the error persists or not. Please see here the last update from SCB
As always, let's keep each other updated on this ticket in order to have a smooth operation and support.
Thank you as always and have a nice weekend.
Best regards,
Francisco
